title: Ramayana Trailer Launches Today at Star-Studded Event in New Delhi Before Global Premiere at Comic-Con
excerpt: Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and the cast of India's most expensive film gather at Bharat Mandapam for the trailer debut, with a San Diego Comic-Con showcase set for July 23.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ramayana: The Epic Begins trailer launches on July 18 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.
  • The film features a star-studded cast, including Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi, with a budget of Rs 4,000 crore.
  • Ramayana will showcase at San Diego Comic-Con, only the second Indian film to do so.
  • Two versions of the trailer received a 'U' certificate from the CBFC on July 15.
  • The film is set for a Diwali 2026 release, with a sequel planned for 2027.
  • The trailer for Ramayana: The Epic Begins debuts at a massive event at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on July 18, with the full cast in attendance.
  • The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Sunny Deol as Hanuman in what is reportedly a Rs 4,000 crore production.
  • Ramayana will become only the second Indian film to receive a major hall showcase at San Diego Comic-Con, with a panel in the 4,800-seat Ballroom 20 on July 23.
  • Two versions of the trailer — both cleared by the CBFC with a 'U' certificate — were certified on July 15.

The most anticipated trailer in Indian cinema arrives today. Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: The Epic Begins will debut its first full trailer at a grand launch event at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Saturday, July 18 — kicking off what the makers are positioning as a global promotional campaign unlike anything Bollywood has attempted before.

The event brings together a cast that reads like an all-star summit of Indian cinema. Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Ram, is confirmed to attend despite reportedly contracting conjunctivitis from his daughter Raha Kapoor in the days before the event. Sai Pallavi (Sita), Ravi Dubey (Lakshman), Rakul Preet Singh (Surpanakha), and Kunal Kapoor (Lord Indra) are confirmed, alongside director Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra.

A Film of Unprecedented Scale

Ramayana has been described as the most expensive Indian film ever produced, with reported budgets ranging from Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000 crore. Malhotra, who is also the Global CEO of DNEG — the Academy Award-winning visual effects powerhouse behind Inception, Interstellar, and Dune — has called the project his dream of over two decades.

The Central Board of Film Certification cleared two versions of the trailer on July 15 with a 'U' certificate — the 4-minute-15-second cut that will screen at the Delhi event. The film itself is set for a Diwali 2026 release (November 6), with a sequel already in production for 2027.

"The panel includes never-before-seen footage, exclusive reveals, live performances, and special giveaways."

— San Diego Comic-Con official listing for the Ramayana panel

Comic-Con History

Five days after the Delhi launch, Ramayana will make history at San Diego Comic-Con. On July 23, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash will take the stage in Ballroom 20 — the convention's second-largest venue, seating approximately 4,800 people — for a one-hour panel that includes exclusive footage and live performances.

The move places an Indian mythological epic alongside the likes of Marvel Studios and major Hollywood franchises that typically dominate Comic-Con's premier venues. Ramayana becomes only the second Indian film to secure a major hall showcase at the event, following Kalki 2898 AD.

The Comic-Con panel is scheduled from 3:15 PM to 4:15 PM PDT on Thursday, July 23 — translating to 3:45 AM IST on Friday, July 24. Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige's presentation, expected to unveil the Avengers: Doomsday trailer, follows two days later in Hall H.

Cast and Characters

The ensemble is one of the most ambitious in Indian cinema. Beyond Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram and Sai Pallavi as Sita, the casting of Kannada superstar Yash as Ravana brings pan-Indian appeal. Sunny Deol — who returns to a major franchise role after Gadar 2 — plays Hanuman. The supporting cast includes Arun Govil, who played Lord Ram in the iconic 1987 television series, along with Lara Dutta, Sheeba Chaddha, Vivek Oberoi, Kajal Aggarwal, and Rakul Preet Singh.

What's Next

Today's event marks the beginning of what will likely be the most extensive promotional campaign in Indian film history. With a November 6 theatrical release and a global marketing push through Comic-Con, the film is targeting audiences well beyond India's borders. For the diaspora, the Comic-Con showcase represents a significant cultural moment — Indian mythology commanding the same global stage as the MCU.
